children: Shares of PNC Infratech dipped 20 per cent to  ₹140 on Tuesday after the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) levied a three-year debarment on Awadh Expressway, a concessionaire SPV of the company.
It also restricted PNC Infratech from bidding for new MoRTH/NHAI projects for the next three years.

However, the company clarified that the action will not impact ongoing projects and said it is exploring legal remedies against the order, adding that any financial implications will be disclosed as clarity emerges.
While the debarment restricts PNC’s ability to bid for new NHAI/MoRTH contracts for three years, its substantial existing order book remains unaffected.

Additionally, the company’s expanding presence in non-road segments (mining, water, airports, Railways, canals) and early diversification into solar/BESS further strengthens the company’s presence across infrastructure sectors beyond its traditional roads business.

PNC Infratech exited FY26 with an unexecuted order book of  ₹19,100 crore, translating to a book-to-bill ratio of nearly 4 times providing multi-year revenue visibility that is largely insulated from the debarment, since existing contracts and concessions are unaffected by a bar on future bidding, said the company.
The order book stood at  ₹15,670 crore across 27 projects as of 30th June’26 stood. NHAI projects constitute only around 30 per cent of the company’s total order book.

The company has, over the past few quarters, been steadily diversifying its revenue beyond the roads portfolio. In mining, PNC is executing a Rs 2,957 crore, five-year contract awarded by South Eastern Coalfields. The company is also expanding into renewable energy, having secured an order from NHPC for a 300 MW ISTS-connected solar power project paired with a 150 MW/600 MWh battery energy storage system with the project expected to start contributing to revenue from FY27.
Combined, the mining and solar-BESS portfolios represent close to  ₹5,000 crore of diversification outside the traditional roads business.
PNC has already secured five new projects in FY27 worth a combined  ₹4,259 crore, including two HAM projects from NHAI and EPC awards from AAI and other authorities.

title: PNC Infratech dips 20% as NHAI bans for 3 years
